messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in fallback events detected for route /v1/chat at 09:12 UTC. fallback_rate=980/s, 5xx_rate=0.9% -> potential routing loop. Incident ID INC-2026-4921 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Paging on-call: @jonas-ops (P1)
jonas-ops: joining. what's the quick scope?
melissa-qa: repro logs show decisions picking variant=gpt-mini-instruct in eu-central-1, then immediately falling back to variant=gpt-mini in us-west-2, then bouncing back. Multiple hops with repeated decision entries.
devon-ml: hmm that variant is not in the policy fallback_order for that route AFAIK. Looking at runtime config - there is a new cost-based selector that prefers gpt-mini-instruct for low-latency targets but the healthscore for that variant is 0.0 in eu-central-1.
maria-sre: observability problem: decision logs here are missing route_tag and decision_trace_id. we only see node and variant. can't correlate to request ids. That makes it impossible for automation to detect repeated hops.
lucy-cs: impact: EU customers on real-time chat reported degraded replies and timeouts. CS tickets queued: EU-77, EU-89. Notified account owners for 5 customers.
jonas-ops: can we apply quick mitigation: pin this route to eu-central-1 and force stable variant gpt-mini for 10m?
devon-ml: yes. but need to also disable the cost-selector temporarily - it's autonomously triggering cross-region choices.
melissa-qa: adding example log snippet showing missing fields:
```
2026-08-03T09:12:22Z decision: route=chat-prod variant=gpt-mini-instruct result=FALLBACK reason=health_unhealthy node=n-54
2026-08-03T09:12:22Z decision: route=chat-prod variant=gpt-mini result=SELECTED node=n-12
```
no route_tag / hop_count / trace id present.
jonas-ops: mitigation steps I'm running now:
1) `redwoodctl policy lock --id chat-prod-policy --set allow_cost_selector=false`
2) `redwoodctl routing override apply --route chat-prod --variant gpt-mini --region eu-central-1 --ttl 600`
3) `redwoodctl cache flush --scope routing --region eu-central-1`
maria-sre: applied override and disabled cost selector. routing cache flush in progress.
devon-ml: I also pushed a small hotfix branch to add route_tag and decision_trace_id into decision logs. PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/4591. It adds fields: route_tag, decision_trace_id, hop_count. Can we canary this?
jonas-ops: canary approved for 2 nodes in eu-central-1. deploy starting.
melissa-qa: watching metrics: fallback rate falling from 980/s to ~40/s within 80s. 5xxs dropping too. RTT for EU region improving.
lucy-cs: CS: sent update to affected customers. No data corruption. Affected customers saw increased latency and some failed responses for ~6 minutes.
maria-sre: note: we observed some stale routing entries from CDN-level cache that caused a few residual double-hop traces. flushed CDN and cleared old entries.
devon-ml: after canary logs are in, we have route_tag+trace ids for new decisions. looking at these, we can confirm loop length up to 4 hops on some requests; loop detector is absent.
jonas-ops: action items for post-incident: 1) add loop-detection max_hops=3 with alert on exceed; 2) ensure decision logs always include route_tag and decision_trace_id; 3) add regression test for cost-selector interacting with health scoring; 4) tighten healthcheck backoff for gpt-mini-instruct variants.
maria-sre: I've created incident ticket INC-2026-4921 with timeline and mitigations. adding runbook notes.
lucy-cs: CS will follow up with impacted accounts and share timeline.
jonas-ops: handing paging over to @melissa-qa for the next 30m. I'll brief the on-call rotation.
melissa-qa: ack. staying on thread.
devon-ml: will open a follow-up PR to add hop_count to the real-time routing metrics so we can trigger alerts when average hop_count > 1.2
maria-sre: closing P1 page for now. monitoring for regressions for next 2 hours. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-4921 acknowledged and resolved by jonas-ops at 09:24 UTC
